title: Provenance record for a single player run on a single task
description: Stored by the framework. Arena code never writes these directly.

resolved_tool_version.description: Optional. The actual installed version of the underlying tool, detected at runtime by the adapter (e.g. 'docpluck-2.4.84'). null when no underlying tool is detectable (e.g. an LLM, whose version is the model id in player_version). Lets the leaderboard rank on the version a score was produced with rather than the static registry label.

input_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonicalized task envelope.

output.description: Player's response, conforming to the arena's output schema.

primary.description: null = task excluded from scoring (e.g., unverifiable ground truth).

findings.description: Optional. Structured failure-mode annotations. See contract/schemas/findings.schema.json for the per-item shape. Held-out task findings are redacted by the runner before persistence — only category + count survive.

task_visibility.description: Optional. Copied from the task envelope by the runner. Defaults to 'held_out' (fail-safe) when the envelope did not declare visibility. Drives report-engine redaction logic.

split.description: Optional. Copied from the task envelope by the runner. 'revealed' records are published un-redacted in the Open Benchmark; 'private' records keep findings redaction. Mirrors task_visibility (revealed<->public, private<->held_out) but names the benchmark suite explicitly for leaderboard partitioning.

provenance.description: Optional. How/when/with-what this record was produced. Populated by the runner. Command is sanitized of any secrets before write.

containment.description: How an agentic-CLI player was contained. null for players with no ambient environment to inherit (HTTP/API, R, library). ABSENT on a CLI record means the record predates containment and ran uncontrolled; see framework/hermetic.py::containment_state. Never backfilled.

profile_version.description: Version of the hermetic profile table. A bump means the containment recipe changed, so records either side are different instruments.

cli_version.description: Version the CLI reported at run time. These auto-update underneath us, so it is recorded per record rather than pinned once.

allow_tools.description: The tool allowlist handed to the CLI. Empty means no tools — the state that closes the answer-key channel.

verified.description: True only when the containment was verified empirically against this CLI (nonce probe), not merely configured.

flags_insufficient.description: True when the CLI's own flags cannot fully close the channel and containment relies on the surrounding environment.

verified_note.description: Human-readable provenance for the verified/flags_insufficient claims.

fingerprint.description: Hash over the containment configuration. A change mints a new instrument rather than silently extending an old player's history.

code_version.description: git SHA of THIS repo when the record was produced. tool_version_detail pins the third-party tool; this pins the framework and scorer that computed the number, so a later scoring fix does not silently make old and new records look alike.

prompt_template_sha256.description: Hash of the prompt template actually used. task_id pins the TASK, not the instructions wrapped around it — and those get edited. Differing hashes on the same task_id mean the records are not comparable.

request_timeout_s.description: Per-call timeout sent. Companion to finish_reason and to timeout-classified errors.

containment.description: How an agentic-CLI player was contained when this record was produced. null for players with no ambient environment to inherit (HTTP/API, R, library calls). ABSENT on a CLI record means the record predates containment entirely (before 2026-08-19), when the player ran inside the repo with its full tool set and could read the answer key — that absence is the ONLY signal distinguishing those records, so they are never backfilled. See framework/hermetic.containment_state.

cli_version.description: The CLI is part of the instrument and auto-updates.

verified.description: A live nonce probe confirmed containment for this binary.

flags_insufficient.description: Measured reading outside its workspace despite every flag it offers; containable only by an OS-level boundary.

usage.description: Token counts reported by a metered API for this task, when the player is one. ABSENT means one of FOUR different things, and they must not be blurred: (a) a local tool player consumed no tokens; (b) a CLI-subscription player is not billed per token; (c) the record is held-out, where prompt_tokens is a near-exact proxy for input document length and is stripped; or (d) the record predates instrumentation on 2026-08-13, when the adapter began reading the `usage` block every provider had been returning all along. Use timestamp_utc and player_type to tell (d) from (a)-(c) — see framework/pricing.py:classify_missing_usage. Absent must never be read as zero. Tokens are persisted rather than a dollar figure because tokens are a measured fact that stays true, while a price is a claim about a list that changes without notice; cost is derived at report time from a dated price table. NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS TRANSPORTS. A CLI-wrapped player (claude --print) is measured at ~46k prompt_tokens for a task an HTTP player does in ~650, because the CLI prepends its own system context and prompt cache. Those tokens are real and really billed on a metered account, but comparing them to a direct API call measures the harness, not the model. Compare tokens only within a transport, and read cross-transport cost with that caveat stated.

cache_read_tokens.description: Anthropic splits the input side into fresh / cache-read / cache-write. prompt_tokens is their SUM; this is the cache-read part, kept separately because it is billed at a different rate and materially changes cost.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache. Billed above the base input rate.

schema_version.description: Run-record shape version. Bumped whenever fields are added. Lets a reader distinguish a field's ABSENCE ('this run predates the field') from its omission ('not applicable to this run') — without it, every gap looks the same. v2 (2026-08-13) added usage, response_meta, and the provenance code_version / prompt_template_sha256 / request_* fields. v3 (2026-08-19) added provenance.containment: an agentic CLI player runs with an ambient environment, and until v3 nothing recorded what that environment was.

response_meta.description: Provider-reported metadata about the call that produced this score. Two independent reviews ranked `finish_reason` the single most important field on the record: a completion truncated at the token limit fails JSON parsing, scores 0.0, and is otherwise indistinguishable from genuine incapability — the benchmark would publish OUR configuration as THEIR failure. Absent for local tool players and for runs before schema v2. SURVIVES held-out redaction (nothing here encodes document length), EXCEPT provider_request_id, which is a pointer into provider logs that do retain the source document.

finish_reason.description: 'stop' = complete. 'length' = TRUNCATED by the token limit; any score on such a record measures our budget, not the model. 'content_filter' = refused.

served_model.description: The model the provider says it ACTUALLY ran. Intent lives in player_version; this is evidence. Never merge them.

served_by.description: The BACKEND that served the call, when the endpoint is a router. OpenRouter fans one model id (openai/gpt-oss-120b) out over CoreWeave, DeepInfra, Novita, Amazon Bedrock and Google, which differ in quantization and serving stack, so served_model alone does not identify what ran. Absent for a direct provider, which is not the same as unknown. Like served_model this is evidence, never intent, and it survives held-out redaction because it encodes nothing about the document.

model_mismatch.description: served_model differs from what we requested — the record is then evidence about a different artifact than its player_id claims.

attempts.description: HTTP attempts including retries. >1 means a transient failure was absorbed; a retried call may have hit a different backend replica, so latency and determinism claims weaken.

system_fingerprint.description: Provider backend build id. Two runs with different fingerprints are not strictly comparable.

service_tier.description: e.g. on_demand vs flex — affects latency and price.

provider_seed.description: The seed the PROVIDER used, which may differ from the one we requested (provenance.seed). Diagnostic only — it is not sufficient to reproduce an output.

provider_request_id.description: Provider-side id for support and dispute resolution. STRIPPED on held-out records.

provider_reported_cost_usd.description: A cost figure the provider's own CLI computed. PROVIDER-REPORTED, never money spent: Claude players run on a Claude Max subscription where a task has no per-token marginal cost, so this is an API-EQUIVALENT figure. Useful for comparing against metered players; misleading if read as spend.
